> I am wondering some formulas in section "Maximum likelihood inference"
> page 23.
> For example, in distribution of x, Q is covariance or precision matrix?
Q is the precision matrix.
> I can not fit distribution of y based on distributions of x and y|x?
in the Gaussian case we have closed integrating out x.
> y is marginal likelihood or marginal distribution?

marginal (in relation o x) distribution of y, but conditional
distribution on the hyper-parameters.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: new tutorial version
parts:
Dear Linh,

The kappa is the scale parameter on SPDE approach.
But, some books use a range parameter that is 1/kappa.
For example, http://www.leg.ufpr.br/mbgbook/

The value sqrt(8v)/kappa is the range in fact.
Because, this is the distance corresponding to
correlations near 0.1

I can clarify it on the text. Thanks!

Best,
Elias.

Hi All,

I have a problem with posterior mean of latent random field. For example in toy model example:

Let X denote the latent random field.

In INLA, chapter 3, the poterior mean of latent random field obtained is: res5$summary.random$i$mean

But in SPDE theory, I got formulas from Finn's papers, I have

X~N(mu, Qx)
Y|X=x ~ N(A x, Qeps)

The posterior distribution for X given Y=y is then given by

X|Y=y ~ N(mupost, Qpost)

Where

Qpost = Qx + A' Qeps A
mupost = mu + Qpost^-1 A' Qeps (y - A mu)

I calculated manually mupost (posterior mean of X), and the result was much different from res5$summary.random$i$mean

Can you please explain me?

Thanks!
